## 7-Day Grocery Basket — Household of 3, $85 Budget

All items are SNAP-eligible. Prices are estimates for a discount/regional chain (Aldi, WinCo, Walmart Grocery). One trip covers the week.

---

### 7-Day Meal Plan

| Day | Breakfast | Lunch | Dinner |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sun** | Oatmeal + banana + milk | PB sandwich + carrot sticks | Baked chicken thighs, rice, roasted carrots |
| **Mon** | Scrambled eggs (2/person) + toast | Leftover chicken + rice bowl | Pasta with tomato-bean sauce (canned tomatoes + canned black beans) |
| **Tue** | Oatmeal + apple | Tuna sandwich + carrot sticks | Potato-onion-bean soup (potatoes, onions, pinto beans, canned tomatoes) |
| **Wed** | Eggs + toast | Leftover soup + bread | Fried rice with frozen mixed veg + 2 eggs |
| **Thu** | Oatmeal + banana | PB sandwich + fruit | Red lentil dal + rice + frozen broccoli |
| **Fri** | Eggs + toast | Tuna rice bowl + cabbage slaw | Cabbage stir-fry with remaining chicken + rice |
| **Sat** | Oatmeal + milk | Bean-rice bowl (seasoned with garlic/onion) | Pasta with lentil-tomato sauce |

---

### Budget Notes

- **$81.10 of $85 used** — the buffer covers forgotten pantry items or a price variance.
- Dried beans (2 lbs) yield ~6 cups cooked; far cheaper per serving than canned. Soak overnight or use the quick-boil method. The 2 cans of black beans provide a fast fallback for busy nights.
- Chicken thighs are ~40% cheaper per pound than breasts and more forgiving to cook. Bone-in adds flavor to soups/rice dishes.
- Buying oats in the canister and rice in the 5 lb bag (vs. single-serve packets) is the single biggest per-meal savings lever.
- Limited transport consideration: everything here has a shelf life of at least 7 days at room temp or in the fridge. Freeze the chicken if you're not using it by Day 3–4.

---

### Nutrition Notes

| Goal | How this basket covers it |
|---|---|
| **Protein** | Eggs, chicken, beans, lentils, tuna, peanut butter — ~60–75 g/person/day achievable |
| **Fiber** | Oats, beans, lentils, cabbage, carrots, potatoes — well above 25 g/day target |
| **Iron** | Lentils + beans are top plant iron sources; pair with tomatoes (vitamin C) to boost absorption |
| **Vitamin A** | Carrots, frozen mixed veg, broccoli |
| **Vitamin C** | Cabbage, broccoli, fresh fruit |
| **Calcium** | Milk covers ~30% DV/cup; supplement with broccoli and beans |
| **Calories** | At ~2,000–2,200 kcal/person/day, the basket is sufficient — oats, rice, and peanut butter are calorie-dense anchors |
| **SNAP/WIC note** | Milk, eggs, and produce overlap with WIC-eligible categories. If the household has WIC, reallocate those dollars toward fresh produce or whole-grain bread upgrades. |

---

**Prep tip for limited transport:** Cook a large batch of rice (full 5 lbs uses ~10 cups water) on Sunday and refrigerate in portions — it reheats in 2 minutes and anchors 4–5 dinners, cutting nightly cook time significantly.
